skill.name: algorithmic-art
skill.description: Create original p5.js generative art with seeded randomness, interactive controls, and a reusable HTML viewer template.
skill.summary: Build reproducible interactive generative art from a concept using p5.js templates and parameter controls.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown code fences, inline template paths, CSS, comments, or JavaScript RegExp.exec used for color parsing. The remaining confirmed issues are low-severity third-party network dependencies for p5.js and Google Fonts in the generated HTML template.

remediation.issue: Generated artifacts load p5.js from a third-party CDN.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle a vetted local copy of p5.js or document that generated artifacts require this remote dependency.

remediation.issue: The viewer template loads Google Fonts from external domains.
remediation.suggestion: Use system fonts or bundle local font assets when privacy-sensitive or offline usage is required.

content.value_statement: Creating polished generative art from a short idea can require design direction, reproducible randomness, and working UI controls. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to produce original p5.js artwork with a reusable interactive viewer.
actual_capabilities: Creates an algorithmic art philosophy before implementation.
Guides p5.js sketches with seeded randomness for reproducible outputs.
Uses an HTML viewer template with seed navigation and parameter controls.
Supports interactive sliders, color controls, reset actions, and seed exploration.
Encourages original algorithms instead of copying existing artists or static templates.
limitations: Generated HTML depends on browser support and p5.js runtime behavior.
The default template loads p5.js and fonts from external CDNs.
Final visual quality still depends on the model implementation and user prompt clarity.
It does not provide image editing, raster post-processing, or asset management workflows.

use_cases.title: Prototype generative art concepts
use_cases.description: Turn a short creative brief into a reproducible p5.js artwork with adjustable parameters.

use_cases.title: Teach creative coding patterns
use_cases.description: Demonstrate seeded randomness, particles, flow fields, and parameter-driven exploration in a browser artifact.

use_cases.title: Build interactive visual experiments
use_cases.description: Create self-contained HTML sketches that users can explore through seeds, sliders, and color controls.

prompt_templates.title: Start a simple seeded artwork
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a first generative art artifact.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an original generative artwork about calm ocean currents. Include a short algorithmic philosophy and a self-contained p5.js HTML artifact with seed controls.

prompt_templates.title: Add interactive controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Create generative art inspired by urban night traffic. Add sliders for density, flow speed, trail length, and noise scale. Keep every seed reproducible.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a concept through variations
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants multiple outputs from one algorithm.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a generative art system for botanical growth. Highlight three interesting seeds and explain how each variation changes the composition.

prompt_templates.title: Build a polished gallery artifact
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a refined interactive viewer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a gallery-quality p5.js artwork around recursive architecture. Use the viewer template, include tuned parameters, color controls, seed navigation, and a concise philosophy.

output_examples.input: Create generative art about wind moving through tall grass.
output_examples.output: A short philosophy about layered motion, followed by an interactive browser artwork with seeded grass-like particles, wind controls, palette controls, and reset actions.

output_examples.input: Make an artwork inspired by crystalline growth.
output_examples.output: A reproducible p5.js artifact where seed changes generate different crystal structures, with controls for branching, density, scale, and color harmony.

output_examples.input: Show me 100 variations from one algorithm.
output_examples.output: A single interactive artwork with seed navigation and guidance for exploring selected seed ranges rather than separate static image files.

best_practices: Start with a clear visual theme and the emotional effect you want the artwork to create.
Ask for seeded randomness and named parameters so results can be repeated and tuned.
Review the generated artifact in a browser and adjust controls for performance and composition.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to imitate a living artist or copy a specific copyrighted artwork.
Do not request a static image when you need an interactive generative system.
Do not remove seed controls if reproducible variations are important.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates original algorithmic art concepts and self-contained p5.js HTML artifacts with interactive controls.

faq.question: Can I reproduce the same artwork later?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill emphasizes seeded randomness so the same seed and parameters produce the same result.

faq.question: Does it require a build step?
faq.answer: No. The intended output is a single HTML artifact that runs in a browser or compatible artifact viewer.

faq.question: Can I adjust the artwork after generation?
faq.answer: Yes. The template supports seed navigation, sliders, color controls, reset actions, and regeneration.

faq.question: Does it work offline?
faq.answer: Not by default. The provided template references p5.js and fonts from external CDNs unless those assets are bundled locally.

faq.question: Is it suitable for commercial artwork?
faq.answer: It can support original concept generation, but you should review the license terms and verify originality before commercial use.
